title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
summary: Find the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of an array.

tests.explain: For example 1, 2, 5, 9 or 1, 2, 4, 6. No increasing subsequence of length 5 exists.
Strictly increasing: equal values can't follow each other, so any single 4 is the longest.
1, 3, 6, 7, 9, 10. The 4, 5, 6 near the end start a shorter chain.

hints: A subsequence keeps the original order but may skip elements. Trying every subset is 2^n, far too slow for 60 numbers.
Let len[i] be the length of the longest increasing subsequence that ends with nums[i]. Which earlier elements could come right before nums[i]?
len[i] = 1 + the largest len[j] over j < i with nums[j] < nums[i] (or 1 if there is none). The answer is the largest len[i] anywhere, not len[n - 1].

complexity.time: O(n²): every index looks back at all earlier ones (O(n log n) with binary search, see below)
